# Piranga, Honey Bee, Red Pyranga, Summer Tanager

Summer Tanager. Piranga rubra.

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [University Park](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque)
- [Biotic Inventory](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico)
- Piranga

[![Piranga illustration banner image](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/d5560ba2-6ea1-419e-b685-a86c307bdd6f/web/piranga-roja.jpg)](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/piranga)

![](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/piranga)

###### Etymology

Piranga, from tijepiranga, a Brazilian indigenous name from the Tupi language, used for some small birds. Rubra, from the Latin ruber, meaning red, reddish.

**Drawings: Daniela Peláez Vélez and Alejandro Arbeláez**

###### Description

It measures approximately 18 cm. The male is entirely bright red, darker dorsally, with brownish wings and tail. The bill is thick and whitish to pale yellow. The female is olive above, with brownish wings and tail, and olive-yellow below. Immature birds: first-year males are identical to the adult female; molting subadults are mottled red and yellow; the juvenile female is duller than the adult female.

###### Ecology

It lives in a variety of environments, from lowlands to mountains, where it is more numerous. It frequents scrubby clearings, shady gardens, forest edges, and open woodland. It can be found alone or in mixed flocks. It feeds on fruit, spiders, and insects. Occasionally, it visits artificial feeders.

###### Distribution

It is a moderately common transient and winter resident species, visiting us from early October to late April. It breeds from the United States to northern Mexico and winters from central Mexico to Bolivia, the Brazilian Amazon, and Suriname. In Colombia, it is distributed up to about 2,700 meters above sea level and is found throughout the country, mostly in the Andean region. During migration season, it can be seen all over the EAFIT University campus.
